0x005dd7b0 XOR EBX,EBX then 0x005dd7b2/0x005dd7b6: EBX is the zero constant and both flags are initialised from it, so BL doubles as the false value throughout the body
0x005dd7ba CMP byte ptr [ESI + 0x102],BL / 0x005dd7c0 JZ 0x005dd7de: a one-byte gate; when it is zero the entire classification is discarded and both flags stay zero

0x005dd7c2 CMP EAX,0x4 / 0x005dd7c5 JA 0x005dd7de: an UNSIGNED bound check on the classification. A negative value is therefore also treated as out of range, which is consistent with the classification port only ever returning 0..4.

A live read of 0x005dd840 returns d4d75d00 d4d75d00 d4d75d00 ced75d00 ced75d00, i.e. entries 0, 1 and 2 all target 0x005dd7d4 and entries 3 and 4 all target 0x005dd7ce, immediately followed by eight cc bytes of padding at 0x005dd854.

0x005dd7ce MOV byte ptr [ESP + 0xc],BL followed by 0x005dd7d2 JMP 0x005dd7d9: classifications 3 and 4 leave the same byte at zero and go straight to the shared tail
0x005dd7d9 MOV byte ptr [ESP + 0x10],0x1: BOTH switch arms converge here, so all five in-range classifications set the first flag. The switch distinguishes only the second flag.

0x005dd7de CMP byte ptr [ESI + 0xd1],BL / 0x005dd7e4 JNZ 0x005dd7ea / 0x005dd7e6 MOV byte ptr [ESP + 0xc],BL: a zero at +0xd1 forces the second flag back to zero. The instruction that would set it is absent, so this field is a one-way inhibit and can never turn the second flag on.

0x005dd812 MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10] then 0x005dd816/0x005dd818: the provider's vtable is loaded and slot +0x7c (index 31) taken
0x005dd81b PUSH ECX / 0x005dd81c PUSH 0x1 / 0x005dd81e MOV ECX,EDI / 0x005dd820 CALL EDX: selector 1 with the first flag, thiscall, two stack arguments

0x005dd822..0x005dd830: the same slot again with selector 2 and the second flag. The vtable is reloaded from the provider rather than reused from a register, and the return value of the first call is not examined.

sdk_correspondence.status: STRONG CANDIDATE FOR THE RECEIVER, UNRESOLVED FOR THE PROVIDER
sdk_correspondence.basis: Six offsets read out of this body and its tail target all match Spore/Editors/EditorUI.h, and the file is the only one examined that carries all six: UTFWin::UILayout mMainUI at +0x14, UTFWin::UILayout mSharedUI at +0x2c, cEditor* mpEditor at +0x5c, bool field_D1 (documented default true) at +0xd1, bool field_102 at +0x102 and bool field_104 at +0x104, with ASSERT_SIZE(EditorUI, 0x12C). The two +0x14/+0x2c members are used as thiscall receivers for a layout element lookup, which is what a pair of UILayout members would be used for, and the +0x5c member is handed to a routine that reads a cEditor-sized object. Independently, the receiver provenance is established at the call site: 0x0058a77b loads cEditor+0x78, which Spore/Editors/Editor.h:266 documents as EditorUI* mpEditorUI.
sdk_correspondence.why_not_established: No vtable for EditorUI was located and this binary has no MSVC RTTI, so the class identity cannot be closed from the binary. The class is recorded as SUPPORTED and is not claimed.

semantic_contract: Non-virtual, void, no-argument member of the editor's UI object. ECX receiver, no stack argument, and the body ends in a tail jump rather than a return, so the frame and the register discipline are resolved before control leaves. The contract is 'recompute whether the paint state is currently available and publish that as a pair of named UI toggle states'. Invariants, in order: (1) ask the object at receiver+0x5c - the SDK's cEditor* mpEditor - for a five-valued paint classification; (2) start both published flags at zero; (3) if the byte at receiver+0x102 is zero, or the classification falls outside 0..4 as compared UNSIGNED, publish nothing and keep both flags at zero; (4) otherwise, via a five-entry jump table at 0x005dd840, set the first flag to 1 for every classification and the second flag to 1 only for classifications 0, 1 and 2, leaving it 0 for 3 and 4; (5) if the byte at receiver+0xd1 is zero, force the second flag back to 0 - this field can only ever clear that flag, never set it; (6) resolve the element with id 0x5b6e484 in mode 1 from the layout at receiver+0x14, and only if that returns null retry the identical lookup against the layout at receiver+0x2c; (7) if a provider was resolved, call its virtual slot +0x7c twice with the arguments (1, first flag) and then (2, second flag), ignoring both return values, and skip both calls entirely if neither layout held the element; (8) tail-transfer to 0x005dc800 with the same receiver, which recomputes its own state rather than receiving this body's flags. The receiver itself is never written, and no global is touched.
classification_rationale: The behaviour is fully determined and unusually well instrumented: all 55 instructions are read, the jump table was read live out of memory rather than inferred from the decompiler, all three callees are resolved to concrete operations from their own decompiled bodies, both flag stores and both branch polarities are explicit, and the two-layout fallback is unambiguous. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC for two named bounds. First, the owning type is bounded: six offsets match Spore/Editors/EditorUI.h uniquely and the receiver's provenance is established from an SDK-named cEditor member, but no vtable exists to close the identity. Second, and more materially, the object behind virtual slot +0x7c was not resolved and the element id 0x5b6e484 appears nowhere in the SDK, so what is actually being published is bounded to 'two named toggle states on a provider found by a hashed id in one of two UI layouts'. That is a real limit on the semantic claim, not a naming quibble, and it is why the classification is bounded rather than strong.
semantic_findings: The five-entry jump table partitions into two arms, not five: entries 0, 1 and 2 all reach 0x005dd7d4 and entries 3 and 4 all reach 0x005dd7ce. Both arms converge on 0x005dd7d9, so the FIRST flag is 1 for every in-range classification and only the SECOND flag is actually classified.

The unsigned bound check at 0x005dd7c5 means a negative classification is also treated as out of range. Since 0x0057aaa0 only returns 0..4, that branch is defensive; the reconstruction keeps the unsigned comparison rather than narrowing it.

The +0xd1 field is a one-way inhibit. The instruction that would set the second flag is absent, so a non-zero +0xd1 merely preserves the switch's decision. Any reading of that field as 'the second feature is available' would be wrong; it can only veto.
The +0x102 field is a master enable for the whole publish step, not a per-flag gate, because a zero there skips the switch entirely and leaves both flags at zero.

The two provider lookups differ only in the layout context: the element id 0x5b6e484 and the mode 1 are re-pushed verbatim at 0x005dd7fd and 0x005dd7ff. That is a 'check the main layout, then the shared layout' pattern, not a two-argument query.

Both virtual calls go to the same slot +0x7c with the same shape and differ only in the selector, 1 then 2, which is what makes 'a setter taking which-toggle and what-state' the supported reading of the slot. The tail target 0x005dc800 issues the identical pair for different element ids, which corroborates the shape without identifying the class.

The exit is a JMP, not a CALL, so the two flags this body computes are not passed to 0x005dc800 in any register. The tail target recomputes the classification from the same receiver, meaning the two functions publish related but independently derived states.

Exactly one of the two inspected call sites null-checks the receiver (0x0058a7c6), and the other does not. Since the body dereferences the receiver at +0x5c, +0x102 and +0xd1 unconditionally, that is an inconsistency in the callers rather than in the body, and it is recorded rather than resolved.

The receiver is not cEditor but the object at cEditor+0x78, which the SDK names EditorUI* mpEditorUI. Attributing this function to cEditor would have been wrong, and the +0x14/+0x2c/+0x5c offsets would not have matched anything in cEditor.

The classification port reads the editor's ResourceKey at +0x48..+0x54 and two bytes at +0x4b3/+0x4b4 that 0x0057f6c0 writes to zero, which is what makes 'paint availability' the supported reading of the 5-valued code. The individual values are not claimed.
unresolved_questions: The owning class. Six offsets match Spore/Editors/EditorUI.h uniquely and the receiver's provenance is cEditor+0x78 = mpEditorUI, but no vtable exists in the typed program and there is no RTTI, so the class is a candidate and not a claim.
The method name; nothing in the binary or the SDK names it.
What object virtual slot +0x7c belongs to, and what that method is called. This is the largest gap: it bounds what the function publishes to 'two named toggle states' without naming either.
What element id 0x5b6e484 denotes. It is absent from every SDK header read, and the sibling ids 0x612efea and 0x612efeb used by the tail target are equally unlabelled.
What the five classification values mean individually. Only the 0-2 versus 3-4 partition that the switch performs is established.
What the +0xd1 and +0x102 fields represent. Their effect on the published flags is read directly, but their intent is not.
Why the same property id 0x55d7ca1 is read both inside the classification port and by the caller at 0x0058a792 immediately after this function returns.
Why only one of the two inspected callers null-checks the receiver.
The twelve uninspected call sites and the flag values their contexts imply, in particular the pair inside cEditor::HandleMessage and the two inside FUN_0058d1c0.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this function. Static analysis cannot show which of the five classification values actually occurs in a live editor session, so the frequency of each published state is unknown.
A trace must resolve the provider that virtual slot +0x7c belongs to, which is the only way to turn 'two named toggle states' into a semantic claim.
A trace must record the live value of the +0x102 enable byte and the +0xd1 inhibit byte, since either can suppress the whole publish step.
A differential test must confirm that the two layouts at +0x14 and +0x2c really are alternatives rather than complementary, i.e. that the fallback path is ever taken.
